# CLI reference

> Every `ocrmd` command, argument and option with its default — read from the typer app in `ocrmd/cli.py`, so it cannot drift from the code.

Run a command as `ocrmd <command>` (the `[project.scripts]` entry point) or `python -m ocrmd <command>`; `ocrmd <command> --help` prints the same options. Defaults shown are the built-in ones: several (`--camera`, `--focus`, `--provider`, `--model`, `--admit`, `--focus-bracket`) follow the [settings](settings.md) when `ocrmd.toml` or an `OCRMD_*` variable changes them. Typer also adds `--install-completion` and `--show-completion` to the top level.

## Global options

Given before the command: `ocrmd --debug verify`.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--debug` | flag | off | print full tracebacks and debug logs |
| `--quiet`, `-q` | flag | off | errors only on the console |

## `scan`

Auto-capture pages from the webcam and process them incrementally.

The shutter fires when the *scene* has settled — still, focused, unobstructed, and with the page outline holding its position — and the page is new and sharp. After a hand or a moved page it waits longer, so a page turn is not captured halfway through. A capture no OCR engine can read is refused rather than made into a page (--no-admit keeps the old behaviour; `ocrmd status` lists what was refused). A soft capture is then re-shot at several lens positions (--focus-bracket) and the extra exposures travel with the page, so text no single focus resolves is re-read from another one instead of guessed at. Preview keys: r rotate, +/- zoom, wasd/arrows pan, f/F focus, 0 reset, space force capture, q quit. The view is saved per camera.

```text
ocrmd scan [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--doc` | text | **required** | document slug |
| `--camera` | text | `0` | index or device-name substring, e.g. c525 |
| `--no-llm` | flag | off | capture + OCR only; fill in the LLM pass later with `ocrmd verify` |
| `--provider` | text | `anthropic` | — |
| `--model` | text | `claude-opus-5-5` | — |
| `--preview` / `--no-preview` | switch | `--preview` | — |
| `--rotate` | integer | — | initial rotation 0/90/180/270 (overrides saved view) |
| `--zoom` | number | — | initial digital zoom, e.g. 2.0 (overrides saved view) |
| `--focus` | text | `continuous` | continuous \| locked \| settle (lock after the first capture) \| off |
| `--admit` / `--no-admit` | switch | `--admit` | refuse automatic captures no OCR engine can read, instead of making a page of them (forced captures are always kept) |
| `--focus-bracket` | text | `auto` | shoot each page at several lens positions: auto (only when the frame is not the sharpest the scene has shown) \| always \| off |
| `--resolution` | text | — | WxH, e.g. 1280x960; default is the largest mode |
| `--title` | text | — | document title (stored in document.yaml) |
| `--tag` | text, repeatable | — | tag for document.yaml; repeatable |
| `--project` | text | — | project name for document.yaml |
| `--duration` | number | — | stop after this many seconds (unattended runs) |
| `--max-pages` | integer | — | stop after this many captures |

## `annotate`

Watch already-scanned pages and fold what you write on the paper into the Markdown.

Hold a scanned page under the camera and underline, highlight, strike through or write a margin note. The page is recognised, the new marks are diffed against the stored crop, and the page file is updated. Underlines and highlights cost nothing — the word positions are already on disk — so only handwriting reaches the model, and only when there is some.

```text
ocrmd annotate [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--doc` | text | **required** | document slug |
| `--camera` | text | `0` | index or device-name substring |
| `--no-llm` | flag | off | skip handwriting; marks still sync free |
| `--provider` | text | `anthropic` | — |
| `--model` | text | `claude-opus-5-5` | — |
| `--dry-run` | flag | off | report what would change, write nothing |
| `--preview` / `--no-preview` | switch | `--preview` | — |
| `--duration` | number | — | — |
| `--max-pages` | integer | — | stop after this many looks |

## `etl`

Extract structured data from a scanned document with a declarative pipeline.

map / filter / extract / reduce / resolve / split / unnest / sample over the document's pages, blocks or figures, each an LLM prompt and an output schema (DocETL's operator model — see ocrmd/etl.py). Every output row carries the page — and, from blocks, the rectangle — it came from; every operator's answers are cached and versioned by its prompt, so changing one operator re-runs one operator. A pipeline may write back into the page files, the page model or document.yaml instead of a spreadsheet (`output.type: frontmatter | layout | document`).

PIPELINE may be a file, or the name of a bundled one: figures, references, glossary, receipts, cases.

```text
ocrmd etl [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--doc` | text | **required** | document slug |
| `--pipeline`, `-p` | path | **required** | the pipeline spec (YAML) |
| `--out` | path | — | write here instead of documents/&lt;doc&gt;/extracted/ |
| `--limit` | integer | — | only the first N pages (try a pipeline cheaply) |
| `--status` | text, repeatable | — | only pages with this status; repeatable |
| `--dry-run` | flag | off | show the prompts and the call count, spend nothing |
| `--no-cache` | flag | off | ignore cached answers and ask again |
| `--export-docetl` | path | — | write a DocETL pipeline + dataset here instead of running |
| `--no-llm` | flag | off | run only the operators that cost nothing |
| `--source` | text | — | pages \| blocks \| figures \| extracted:&lt;name&gt; (overrides the spec) |
| `--score` | path | — | a JSON list of expected rows; report precision/recall on --score-key |
| `--score-key` | text | `name` | the field --score matches rows on |
| `--provider` | text | `anthropic` | — |
| `--model` | text | `claude-opus-5-5` | — |

## `read`

Read one region of a page harder than the page itself was read.

The same thing the web UI does when you drag a box on a page image: the rectangle is cut out of the flat rendering, enlarged on its own terms and re-read. Nothing is stored — this answers "what does that word say", and the answer goes to you, not into the page file.

```text
ocrmd read [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--doc` | text | **required** | document slug |
| `--page` | integer | **required** | page sequence |
| `--region` | text | `0,0,1,1` | x,y,w,h as fractions of the page (0-1) |
| `--llm` | flag | off | also ask the model about this region (costs tokens) |
| `--ask` | text | — | what to ask about the region, instead of 'transcribe it' |
| `--save` | path | — | write the enlarged crop here, as it was read |
| `--provider` | text | `anthropic` | — |
| `--model` | text | `claude-opus-5-5` | — |

## `send`

Hand a page you have read to a destination — a study platform, a knowledge base, anything that speaks the sink contract (ocrmd/sinks.py; `ocrmd sinks` lists what is configured).

The text goes out, the photograph does not: the receiver gets ocrmd's *reconciled* reading, the page's provenance (document, page, page id, both agreement scores, a link back to the image) and the document's catalogue entry. Nothing here is written and no stage is marked — the same contract as `ocrmd read`. `--region` reads a box first and sends *that* reading, which is what to reach for when one item on a crowded page came out badly.

```text
ocrmd send [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--doc` | text | **required** | document slug |
| `--page` | integer | **required** | page sequence |
| `--to` | text | `""` | destination name (see `ocrmd sinks`); may be omitted when only one is configured |
| `--option`, `-o` | text, repeatable | — | key=value for one of the receiver's options; repeatable |
| `--region` | text | — | x,y,w,h fractions: read this box first and send that reading |
| `--dry-run` | flag | off | show the envelope that would be sent, send nothing |

## `export`

Write a document in another shape: the built Markdown, plain text, one JSON object, or one JSON object per page. Every shape keeps the page ids, so a consumer can always come back to the photograph.

```text
ocrmd export [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--doc` | text | — | document slug; default every document |
| `--format`, `-f` | text | `md` | md \| txt \| json \| jsonl |
| `--out` | path | — | write here instead of &lt;root&gt;/export/&lt;slug&gt;/&lt;slug&gt;.&lt;fmt&gt; (one document only) |

## `index`

Rebuild the search index from the page files. Search does this on its own for pages whose file changed; this is for after restoring a backup, or to be sure.

```text
ocrmd index [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--doc` | text | — | document slug; default every document |
| `--force` | flag | off | re-read every page file, not just the changed ones |

## `reconstruct`

Rebuild pages from their Markdown as SVG + LaTeX, and score them against the original crop.

The round trip is the check: anything the transcription lost — a heading flattened, a table turned to prose, a figure nobody mentioned — shows up as a difference between the rebuilt page and the photograph it came from. `fidelity` is that difference as one number, 0 to 1.

```text
ocrmd reconstruct [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--doc` | text | **required** | document slug |
| `--page` | integer | — | one page sequence; default every page |
| `--out` | path | `reconstructed` | directory for the .svg/.tex/.png |
| `--pdf` | flag | off | also compile the LaTeX (needs a TeX engine) |
| `--review` | flag | off | ask the model what the rebuild lost (costs tokens) |
| `--provider` | text | `anthropic` | — |
| `--model` | text | `claude-opus-5-5` | — |

## `verify`

(Re)run missing/stale stages — e.g. the LLM pass for pages scanned with --no-llm or while offline.

Without --refresh a completed LLM pass is always reused, whatever prompt version produced it: a version bump must never silently spend tokens on a whole book.

```text
ocrmd verify [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--doc` | text | — | — |
| `--flagged-only` | flag | off | re-run only pages already marked flagged |
| `--refresh` | flag | off | also re-run pages whose LLM pass used an older prompt version (costs tokens) |
| `--batch` | flag | off | send the LLM pass through the Batches API (half price, up to hours of latency) |
| `--wait` / `--no-wait` | switch | `--wait` | with --batch: poll until the batch ends and collect it |
| `--collect` | flag | off | collect batches submitted earlier with --batch --no-wait |
| `--provider` | text | `anthropic` | — |
| `--model` | text | `claude-opus-5-5` | — |

## `reprocess`

Re-derive pages from the raw captures with the current preprocessing pipeline.

Use after upgrading ocrmd: page ids come from the processed image, so improved cropping, rotation or spread-splitting produces different pages. Cached OCR/LLM results for the old pages are discarded (the LLM pass re-runs and costs tokens); raw captures are never touched. Human-edited page files are also replaced — export them first if they matter.

```text
ocrmd reprocess [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--doc` | text | — | — |
| `--no-llm` | flag | off | — |
| `--provider` | text | `anthropic` | — |
| `--model` | text | `claude-opus-5-5` | — |
| `--yes`, `-y` | flag | off | skip the confirmation prompt |

## `review`

Step through flagged disagreements: pick the OCR or the LLM reading, type your own, or skip.

A page with no disagreements left is signed off as `reviewed`; the pipeline then keeps its body on later runs. Answers: o=OCR l=LLM t=type k=keep unresolved s=skip page q=quit. (The web UI — `ocrmd serve` — does the same with the page image alongside.)

```text
ocrmd review [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--doc` | text | **required** | document slug |
| `--who` | text | `reviewer` | reviewer name recorded in the page |
| `--list` | flag | off | print the open disagreements and exit |

## `delete`

Delete pages (or a whole document): database rows, artifacts, page files — and the raw capture when no page refers to it any more. Irreversible; the web UI offers the same with confirmations.

```text
ocrmd delete [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--doc` | text | **required** | document slug |
| `--page`, `-p` | integer, repeatable | — | sequence number(s) to delete; repeatable |
| `--whole-capture` | flag | off | also delete the other half of each spread |
| `--all` | flag | off | delete the whole document |
| `--keep-raw` | flag | off | keep raw captures that nothing refers to any more |
| `--yes`, `-y` | flag | off | skip the confirmation prompt |

## `ocr-bench`

Score local OCR against the LLM transcriptions in the store (bag-of-words F1 per page).

Uses every page that has a legible model transcription; the numbers that chose the default engines are in ocr.py. Run it after installing an engine or changing the camera to see whether it paid off.

```text
ocrmd ocr-bench [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--doc` | text | — | — |
| `--engines`, `-e` | text | — | engine set to measure, e.g. apple_vision or apple_vision+rapidocr (default: configured) |
| `--compare` | flag | off | measure every installed engine alone and every pair |
| `--limit` | integer | — | only the first N reference pages |
| `--verbose`, `-v` | flag | off | one line per page |
